literal: Death (acc.) by hand is like calling, to the powerful the powerless harm doing.
translation: For the powerless to do harm to the powerful is like beckoning Death with their own hands.
modern: வலியற்றவர்கள் வலிமை மிக்கவர்களுக்குத் தீங்கு செய்வது, தங்கள் கைகளால் எமனை அழைப்பதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the folly of provoking those who are stronger than oneself. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to the powerful who can accomplish things, while 'ஆற்றாதார்' refers to those lacking such power. By doing harm ('இன்னா செயல்') to the mighty, the weak are essentially bringing destruction upon themselves. The poet uses the striking image of beckoning Death ('கூற்றத்தை') with one's own hand ('கையால் விளித்தற்றால்') to illustrate the suicidal nature of such an act.
